title: Git Basics: Your First Repository
learning_objectives: Install and configure Git on your local machine
Initialize a Git repository and understand the .git directory
Use git add to stage changes and understand the staging area concept
Use git status and git log to inspect repository state
Create a README.md file for the CatchBook project
outline: Installing Git: Verify installation with git --version
Configuring Git: user.name and user.email (why this matters)
Creating your first repository: git init for CatchBook
Understanding the three states: working directory, staging area, repository
The staging area: Why git add exists (selective commits)
Making your first commit: git commit with meaningful messages
Viewing history: git log, git log --oneline, git log --graph
Checking status: git status and interpreting output
Hands-on exercise: Create CatchBook repo structure with README

catchbook_context.deliverable: CatchBook Git repository with README.md describing the project

criteria: Git is installed and configured with correct user info
CatchBook repository initialized with git init
At least 2 commits made with descriptive messages
Can use git status to check repository state
Can use git log to view commit history

resources.title: Pro Git Book - Chapter 2: Git Basics
Git Tutorial for Beginners: Learn Git in 15 Minutes

professor_constraints: Walk through each command step-by-step with expected output
Show common errors and how to interpret them (e.g., 'not a git repository')
Emphasize commit message best practices early (imperative mood, 50 char limit)
Use CatchBook README as the practice file (makes it real)
Include checkpoint after staging area explanation (common confusion point)
Demonstrate git status after every operation to show state changes
Address 'why do I need to add before commit?' question proactively
